description: Countries and their cities for category-key synthetic dataset. Variable K per country for HC evaluation.

rivers: The Amazon River flows through South America and is the largest river by discharge volume in the world.
The Nile River extends approximately 6,650 kilometers through northeastern Africa.
The Mississippi River is the second-longest river in North America, flowing 3,730 kilometers.
The Danube River flows through ten countries in Central and Southeastern Europe.
The Yangtze River is the longest river in Asia and the third-longest in the world.
The Ganges River flows through India and Bangladesh and is considered sacred in Hinduism.
The Rhine River flows through six countries in Western and Central Europe.
The Volga River is the longest river in Europe, flowing through central Russia.
The Mekong River flows through six countries in Southeast Asia.
The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, reaching depths of 220 meters.
The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years.
The Thames River flows through southern England including London.
The Seine River winds through Paris and northern France.
The Tigris River flows through Turkey and Iraq.
The Euphrates River is the longest river in Western Asia.
The Zambezi River features Victoria Falls, one of the largest waterfalls in the world.

The Indus River flows through Pakistan and is vital for irrigation.
The Rio Grande forms part of the border between the United States and Mexico.
The Ob River in Russia is one of the longest rivers in the world.
The Yenisei River flows through central Siberia to the Arctic Ocean.
The Niger River is the third-longest river in Africa.
The Parana River flows through Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina.
The Mackenzie River is the longest river system in Canada.
The Lena River flows through eastern Siberia to the Laptev Sea.
The Don River flows through Russia and empties into the Sea of Azov.
The Elbe River flows through the Czech Republic and Germany.
The Po River is the longest river in Italy.
The Tagus River is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula.
The Oder River forms part of the border between Germany and Poland.
mountains: Mount Everest stands at 8,849 meters and is the highest peak on Earth.

Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa at 5,895 meters.
Mont Blanc is the highest peak in the Alps at 4,808 meters.
Mount McKinley, also known as Denali, is the highest peak in North America.
Mount Fuji is an active volcano and the highest peak in Japan at 3,776 meters.
Mount Elbrus is the highest peak in Europe at 5,642 meters.
The Matterhorn is one of the most iconic peaks in the Alps.
Aconcagua is the highest mountain in both the Southern and Western Hemispheres.
Mount Rainier is an active stratovolcano in Washington State.
Mount Kenya is the second-highest mountain in Africa.
The Andes mountain range extends along the western coast of South America.
The Himalayas contain the highest peaks on Earth including Mount Everest.
The Rocky Mountains extend over 4,800 kilometers through North America.
The Alps stretch across eight European countries.
Kangchenjunga is the third-highest mountain in the world.
Lhotse is the fourth-highest mountain in the world at 8,516 meters.
Mount Olympus is the highest mountain in Greece at 2,917 meters.
Mount Etna is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.
The Pyrenees form a natural border between France and Spain.
Table Mountain is a flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town.
Mount Cook is the highest peak in New Zealand at 3,724 meters.
Pikes Peak is a famous mountain in the Colorado Rockies.
Mount Vesuvius destroyed the ancient Roman city of Pompeii.
The Carpathian Mountains form an arc across Central and Eastern Europe.
Mount Blanc is the highest summit in Western Europe.
The Atlas Mountains stretch across Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia.
Mount Kosciuszko is the highest peak on the Australian mainland.
Ben Nevis is the highest peak in the British Isles at 1,345 meters.
The Ural Mountains form a natural boundary between Europe and Asia.
landmarks: The Great Wall of China stretches over 21,000 kilometers across northern China.
The Eiffel Tower stands 330 meters tall in the heart of Paris.
The Colosseum in Rome was the largest amphitheater in the Roman Empire.
The Taj Mahal in Agra was built as a mausoleum by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
Machu Picchu is an ancient Incan citadel set high in the Andes Mountains.
The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Stonehenge is a prehistoric monument located in Wiltshire, England.
The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States.
The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis in Greece.
Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world, located in Cambodia.
The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts center in Australia.
Christ the Redeemer is a large Art Deco statue atop Corcovado Mountain in Rio.
Petra is a historical city in Jordan known for its rock-cut architecture.
The Alhambra is a palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain.
The Forbidden City in Beijing was the Chinese imperial palace for 500 years.
Chichen Itza is a large pre-Columbian archaeological site in Mexico.
The Acropolis of Athens contains the remains of several ancient buildings.
Hagia Sophia in Istanbul was built as a cathedral in 537 AD.
The Tower of London has served as a royal palace, prison, and treasury.
The Kremlin in Moscow is the official residence of the President of Russia.
Big Ben is the nickname for the Great Bell at the Palace of Westminster.
The Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin.
The Golden Gate Bridge spans the Golden Gate strait in San Francisco.
The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world at 828 meters.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa has a tilt caused by soft ground on one side.

The Blue Mosque in Istanbul is known for its blue tiles adorning its interior.
The Sagrada Familia in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882.
Mount Rushmore features the carved faces of four American presidents.
The Great Barrier Reef is the worlds largest coral reef system.
country_facts: Australia is both a country and a continent, known for its unique wildlife.
Canada is the second-largest country by total area in the world.
Russia spans eleven time zones across Europe and Asia.
The United States has fifty states and is the third most populous country.
Brazil covers nearly half of South America's total land area.
The economy of China has grown rapidly since market reforms in 1978.
India is the worlds most populous country with over 1.4 billion people.
Germany has the largest economy in Europe and is a major exporter.
France is known for its contributions to art, philosophy, and cuisine.
Japan has the third-largest economy in the world by nominal GDP.
The United Kingdom consists of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
Italy is home to more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.
Spain was a global empire during the 15th and 16th centuries.
South Korea is known for its technological innovation and pop culture.
Mexico has the largest number of Spanish speakers in the world.

Poland has undergone major economic transformation since 1989.

South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein.
Thailand was never colonized by a European power.
Vietnam has one of the fastest-growing economies in Southeast Asia.
Ethiopia is the oldest independent country in Africa.
The Philippines is an archipelago of over 7,000 islands in Southeast Asia.

Pakistan is the fifth most populous country in the world.
oceans_seas: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.
The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean in the world.
The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean and the warmest.
The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the five major oceans.
The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica and is the newest defined ocean.

The Caribbean Sea is located between Central America, South America, and the Caribbean islands.
The South China Sea is an important shipping route in Southeast Asia.
The Red Sea separates Africa from the Arabian Peninsula.
The Black Sea is connected to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus.
The Caspian Sea is the worlds largest inland body of water.
The Baltic Sea is surrounded by Scandinavian and Northern European countries.
The North Sea lies between Great Britain and Scandinavia.

The Arabian Sea lies between the Indian subcontinent and the Arabian Peninsula.
The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay in the world.

The Bering Sea connects the Pacific and Arctic Oceans.

deserts: The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering most of North Africa.
The Gobi Desert stretches across northern China and southern Mongolia.
The Arabian Desert covers most of the Arabian Peninsula.
The Kalahari Desert spans Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa.

The Sonoran Desert spans parts of the United States and Mexico.

The Great Victoria Desert is the largest desert in Australia.
The Thar Desert lies on the border of India and Pakistan.

The Karakum Desert covers most of Turkmenistan.

historical_events: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century.
The French Revolution of 1789 fundamentally changed European politics.
World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918 and involved major world powers.
The Roman Empire at its peak controlled most of Europe and the Mediterranean.
The Renaissance was a cultural movement that began in Italy in the 14th century.
The Silk Road connected China with the Mediterranean for centuries.
The printing press was invented by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440.
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 marked the end of the Cold War era.
The Ancient Egyptian civilization lasted for over three thousand years.
The Mongol Empire was the largest contiguous land empire in history.
The Age of Exploration began in the 15th century with Portuguese voyages.
The American Revolution established the United States as an independent nation.
The Ottoman Empire lasted from 1299 to 1922 and spanned three continents.
The Black Death killed an estimated one-third of Europes population.
The Space Race between the US and USSR peaked with the 1969 Moon landing.
The Scientific Revolution of the 16th and 17th centuries transformed understanding of nature.
The Treaty of Westphalia in 1648 established the modern concept of nation-states.
The abolition of slavery was a major social movement of the 19th century.
The Green Revolution increased agricultural production in developing countries.
The invention of the internet in the late 20th century transformed global communication.
languages_culture: Mandarin Chinese is the most spoken language in the world by number of native speakers.
English is the most widely spoken language globally when including non-native speakers.
Arabic is spoken across the Middle East and North Africa.
Hindi is one of the official languages of India and is widely spoken in South Asia.
Spanish is the official language in 20 countries around the world.
French is spoken on five continents and is an official language of the United Nations.
Portuguese is the official language of Brazil, Portugal, and several African nations.
Russian is the most widely spoken Slavic language.
Japanese uses three writing systems: hiragana, katakana, and kanji.
Korean has a unique alphabet called Hangul, created in the 15th century.
Latin was the language of the Roman Empire and influenced many modern languages.
Sanskrit is one of the oldest known languages in the world.
Swahili is a widely spoken language in East and Central Africa.
Turkish belongs to the Turkic language family and uses the Latin alphabet since 1928.

Polish is the most widely spoken West Slavic language.

science_nature: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.

The periodic table organizes chemical elements by atomic number.
Gravity is the force of attraction between objects with mass.
Evolution by natural selection was proposed by Charles Darwin.
The water cycle describes the continuous movement of water on Earth.
Plate tectonics explains the movement of Earths lithospheric plates.
The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons.
Quantum mechanics describes the behavior of particles at the atomic scale.
The greenhouse effect traps heat in Earths atmosphere.
Mitosis is the process of cell division that produces identical daughter cells.
The electromagnetic spectrum includes radio waves, visible light, and X-rays.
Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.
Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is extremely strong.
The theory of relativity was developed by Albert Einstein in the early 20th century.
Ecosystems include all living organisms and their physical environment.
Nuclear fusion powers the Sun by combining hydrogen atoms into helium.
Tectonic plates move at rates of a few centimeters per year.
The human genome contains approximately 20,000 protein-coding genes.
